This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.565 of 2020 registered at Police Station Gole Ka Mandir, Gwalior (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 406 of IPC.

entities.text: Police Station Gole Ka Mandir, Gwalior
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Applicant is in judicial custody since 18-04-2024.

As per the case of prosecution, Rajendra Pal Singh Sengar submitted a hand-written complaint to SHO, PS Gole Ka Mandir, District Gwalior on 18-2- 2020 inter alia stating that his neighbour Government teacher Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria(applicant) approached him with a proposal for Shiv Kumar Singh Bhadouria vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116691151/
1 sale of a plot at Pinto Park.

entities.text: Shiv Kumar Singh Bhadouria vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He paid Rs.3,50,000/- to Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria as advance in presence of Naresh Singh and others.
Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria got an agreement to sell executed by Rajendra Agrawal on 04-07-2013 for a plot ad- measuring 2100 sq.ft on payment of Rs.35 lacs.
It was agreed that remaining five lac rupees would be paid to Rajendra Agrawal through Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria at the time of registration of sale deed.
On 27-08-2013, Rajendra Agrawal got executed one consent deed of 1/3rd part of plot from Amar Singh which was found to be forged.
A dispute arose at the time of possession and construction of boundary wall on the plot, therefore, he published a public notice in daily newspaper ''Dainik Bhaskar'' on 24-10-2013.
He demanded return of advance money from Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria.

Shivkumar Singh paid him Rs.3,00,000/-
through cheque on 08-07-2013 and Rs.1,00,000/- on 16-07-2013.

After creating social pressure,
Shivkumar Singh gave him three cheques of Rs.5 lac each on 19-09-2014 but he has not paid remaining sixteen lac rupees till date.
Shivkumar Singh is threatening to involve him in a false case.
Entire transaction was conducted by Shivkumar Singh.
Shivkumar has committed cheating with him.
Matter was enquired by SHO, Gole Ka Mandir.
After enquiry, FIR at Crime No.565 of 2020 was registered for offence punishable under Sections 420, 406 of IPC against Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria and Rajendra Agrawal.
Statements of witnesses were recorded.
Relevant documents were seized.
Rajendra Pal Singh Sengar was arrested.
The agreement to sell, power of attorney, consent deed, copies of cheques and hand-written receipts were seized at his instance.
On completion of investigation, Final Report was submitted against Rajendra Agrawal on 08-5-2021 pending the investigation against Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria under Section 173(8) of CrPC.
After receipt of report of hand-writing expert, notice under Section 41-A of CrPC was issued to Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria.
The cheque relating to transaction between the complainant and Shivkumar Singh was seized along-with the bank statement.
The relevant revenue papers were requisitioned from Halka Patwari.
On completion of investigation, supplementary charge-sheet was filed against Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria for offence punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC on 05-09-2023.
The Court directed to seize the original documents.

After completion of further investigation,
supplementary challan was again filed on 10-04-2024.

Learned Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Gwalior took cognizance for offence punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC against Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria.
After rejection of application u/S 437 of CrPC filed on behalf of Shivkumar Singh Bhadauria, he was taken into custody vide order dated 18-04-2024.
Applicant is in custody ever since.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the agreement to sell was executed by Rajendra Agrawal in favour of Rajendra Pal Singh Sengar.
Learned Counsel referring to agreement dated 04-07-2013, submits that the recital of agreement shows payment of consideration amount to Rajendra Agrawal.
Further, the backside of first page of the agreement mentions the receipt of Rajendra Agrawal with reference to agreement of sale.
All other documents were executed by Rajendra Agrawal.
Applicant is not executant or witness in any of the documents.
Only allegation against the applicant is that he was mediator in the transanction.

Learned Counsel further contends that the last transaction with regard to payment of money as reflected from the material on record is dated 19-09-2014 wherein, one cheque for amount of Rs.5 lac was given by Shivkumar Singh Bhadoriya in favour of complainant Rajendra Pal Singh Sengar.
This FIR was registered six years thereafter.
Learned Counsel contends that it is a matter of civil transaction between the parties.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel further contends that the applicant appeared before the Investigation Officer in compliance with the notice under Section 41-A of the CrPC.
The Investigation Officer did not arrest the applicant.
The supplementary chargesheet was filed twice without arresting the applicant.

Learned JMFC in contravention of directives of the Apex Court in case of Aman Preet Singh vs. CBI through Director, (2021) AIR (SC) 4154, Para- 11 and Siddharth vs.
State of Uttar Pradesh & Another, 2021 SCC Online SC 615, had taken the applicant into custody.

sentences.text: There was no allegation that applicant has not cooperated in the investigation or he may not tamper with the evidence.
Learned Counsel further submits that the applicant is a Government Teacher.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
No further custodial interrogation is needed in the matter.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by the applicant as both the parties relate to same socio-economic status.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.

P e r contra, learned Counsel for the State ably assisted by learned Counsel for the complainant contends that the main allegations in the FIR and statements of the witnesses are against the applicant.
The applicant was instrumental in getting the agreement to sell executed in favour of the complainant relating to such land which was later found to be of ownership of other person.
Rajendra Agrawal was paid money on guarantee of applicant.
Some part of consideration was paid through applicant to Rajendra Agrawal.
Therefore, involvement of applicant in the alleged transaction cannot be ruled out.
Applicant was not available for investigation till 2023.
Applicant may not be extended the benefit of bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
